recommendations.text: For the products for which Italy has a protected zone, all producers should be registered, the checks required in Council Directive 77/93/EEC carried out and a plant passport issued when the requirements are met and the products are moved within the protected zone. The Italian authorities are asked to amend the relevant Italian legislation and make the execution coherent with the requirements laid down in Council Directive 77/93/EEC.

Given the serious doubts on its enforcement, and the associated phytosanitary risks, it is suggested to the Italian authorities to reconsider the application of the provisions of local movement. As the provisions are laid down as a "may"-clause in Directive 77/93/EEC, transposition in the Italian legislation is not mandatory. In EC legislation

The Italian authorities are strongly in favour of deletion of the articles in Council Directive 77/93/EEC dealing with local movement and the related items. As a second option mandatory registration and checks can replace the present provisions.
If the provisions are maintained, the Commission should draft clear definitions and monitor its uniform application in the Member States. 5

To the Italian veterinary authorities: The mission team recommends: 6.1.1. that consideration be given to the implications of legal procedures which may result in delays in the destruction of animals involved in an outbreak of a List A disease; 6.1.2. that measures be put in place in Italy to ensure the effective cleaning and disinfection of empty transport vehicles travelling between the non-accredited and the accredited zones in connection with the purchase of accredited breeding stock.

To the veterinary authorities of the Region of Lombardy: The mission team recommends: 6.2.1. that the epidemiological enquiry be continued with all necessary intensity until a positive source of the original infection is identified. In particular, further investigations are required in farms related by ownership to the primary outbreak holding in order to eliminate any possible epidemiological links; 6.2.2. that, where the stamping out of a List A disease is concerned, sufficient resources are allocated to ensure that the epidemiological enquiries are carried out with the greatest possible expedition; 6.2.3. that, in all cases where preventative slaughter is carried out, samples for epidemiological investigation should always be collected. 10

To the Commission services: The mission team recommends: 6.3.1. that a follow-up mission be sent to evaluate in detail the Italian national programme for the eradication of swine vesicular disease; 6.3.2. that the Commission services study as a matter of urgency all aspects of cleaning and disinfection of transport vehicles with a view to issuing guidelines with European Union-wide application; 6.3.3. that the Commission services consider the possibility of a decision requiring that a period of at least thirty days should separate the introduction of pigs to, and any movement of pigs from, a holding. 11

audits.title: Bovine Brucellosis eradication programme, bovine tuberculosis eradication programme and the enzootic bovine leucosis programme

recommendations.text: Strategic national financial planning should be instituted so that funds earmarked for veterinary use in the regions are used for veterinary purposes.

An expert group on all aspects of brucellosis eradication and control in buffaloes should be convened and a realistic and practical programme developed and submitted to the Commission for approval. 7.2. To the Commission services : 7.2.1. The possible late payment of reactor compensation to owners should be investigated on a national basis and if it is found to be widespread suitable action should be taken. This should be made a condition for the approval of future disease eradication programmes. 7.2.2. To consider making approval of future eradication plans conditional to the submission of a strategic national financial plan for the programmes.

To require the opinion of the Scientific Veterinary Committee on : a) validity of the serological tests for brucellosis in buffaloes; b) validity of the tuberculin test in buffaloes; c) significance of the EBL virus infection in buffaloes.
To review eventually the legislation relating to the three diseases on the basis of the opinion of the Scientific Veterinary Committee and the program referred to in 7.1.2.
The Commission services should organise an inspection mission to evaluate progress in due time. 13

audits.title: Monitoring of the progress of the Brucella melitensis eradication programme

recommendations.text: To launch an urgent information campaign to potential consumers of contaminated milk products and to take the appropriate measures in the farms, retail shops and restaurants as a matter of urgency.

To take the appropriate actions in order to provide the LVS in Calabria with an appropriate service in the ARS and to ensure that the resources required are sufficient to fulfil the goal of the BM eradication programme.

To submit a request to the Commission for approval of the derogation of non registration of small sheep and goat flocks (foreseen in Article 3(2) of this Council Directive 92/102/EEC, following the procedure described in art. 18 of Council Directive 90/425/EEC).
To ensure that the review of data collection is carried out as soon as possible in order to improve the clarity.

To elaborate a programme for the regions where the BM situation is not under control which would include the following steps: · statistical epidemiological study, with the collaboration of the LVS. This study should be followed by: · a verification procedure of compliance with the approved eradication programme so that possible deficiencies can be properly identified and corrective measures taken. · Revision of the current eradication programme, laying down clear strategies for the different situations, which would include the possibility of vaccination. This schedule must be sent to the Commission within 30 working days of finalising the report and should comprise deadlines for each step.
To ensure that the operations in the local laboratories of the IZ are properly controlled by the ISS in the shortest time possible.

To consider the problems reported by the farmers in eliminating the reactors and to inform the Commission Services of the possible solutions as soon as possible. 7.2. To European Commission Services: 1) A follow up mission should be carried out in the same regions and in other regions with high prevalence of BM reported. 2) Future decisions on BM eradication programmes presented by Italy should consider the findings of the present report. 22 23

Recommendations to the Member State (1) The competent authorities of Italy should take immediate action to adopt a Salmonella control programme in poultry in accordance with the relevant Community legislation. In any case, such programme should be made compulsory for the industry in the cases for which this is foreseen by Directive 92/117/EEC. (2) The competent authorities of Italy should rectify without delay the deficiencies found in the different establishments visited and referred to under the different conclusions in Section 5 above. (3) The competent authorities of Italy should take appropriate measures to rectify any deficiencies of the same type found during this mission in all the other approved plants in Italy. (4) The competent authorities should address the weaknesses in the supervisory systems at the different levels.

Within three months after the receipt of the final report the competent authorities of Italy should inform the Commission of the progress and result of the measures taken including a timetable for completion of measures and actions still outstanding at that time. PAG 35 Mission report Italy - poultry (4 - 15.10.1999) DG(SANCO)/1212/1999-MR Final ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)1212/1999 Competent Authorities (CA) response to the recommendations in the report 1. The CA reiterate that the outline decree for the application of Annex III to Directive 92/117/EEC has been prepared and is being examined by the bodies responsible for assessment and verification for the purpose of subsequent forwarding for signature by the Minister. The provisions are to be issued in the year 2000. 2. As for the improvements to organisation, harmonisation of procedures and specific application of certain aspects relating to veterinary supervision, the CA state that they will shortly hold a meeting with the veterinary service of the Regions to address the results and shortcomings highlighted during the Community inspection. Subsequently, on the basis of the above, they undertake to issue instructions to the local veterinary service. According to this statement, preliminary arrangements are being made for a ministerial circular on "own checks", veterinary supervision and official checks on "own checks". Arrangements will be made shortly for standardised inspection reports. The CA declare that they will issue further explanations and instructions to the operators and local veterinary services in the light in particular of the additional assessments made during the Community inspection. In relation to animal protection during transport, full harmonisation of the operational conduct between veterinary services is said to be underway including detailed procedures for recording and filing of the data on the checks carried out. With reference to the specific welfare problems in one of the plants visited, the statement specifies that the veterinary service of the establishment took the appropriate measures in respect of the transport company on 8 October 1999 to ensure restoration of the correct transport conditions. In relation to protection of animals at the time of slaughter, the CA stated that they are acquiring further data and information on this subject also with a view to possible assessment and definition by the Scientific Committee of the most appropriate technical features for stunning equipment. With regard to the protection of the laying hens in battery cages, the CA declare that they are now preparing appropriate guidelines with a view to improving the harmonisation of operating procedures throughout the whole country. recommendations.text: In accordance with Article 7, paragraph 3 of Commission Decision 98/139/EC, the Italian authorities must thoroughly investigate the general situation in relation to the implementation of Council Directives 91/495/EEC and 92/45/EEC in all Italian game establishments. The Italian authorities shall notify the Commission within 3 months of the receipt of the final report of this mission of the results of the checks and of the measures taken to remedy the situation. The investigation should concentrate on the official controls during intake, processing, storage and despatch of game meat and on control of health marked labelling in order to ensure traceability of product through establishments and correct labelling and documentation of product place on the market or exported.
To notify the Commission of the effective date of legislation transposing Council Directive 96/93/EC into Italian law.
The existing programme of consultation with the authorities of third countries on the preparation of export certification should be continued.

To increase the number of inspections of establishments carried out by the central authority in order to ensure consistent application of Community requirements in relation to the approval of establishments and the maintenance of standards in establishments. 19 26/01/01 - 30851

To provide a written response to the Commission services, within 3 months from the receipt of the final report, detailing a programme, including a timetable, for the centralised co-ordination of the training of the staff in the veterinary services. This programme should include a system for identification of best practice and for dissemination of such practice by means of guidelines and training courses. 8.2. To the Commission Services: 8.2.1 To monitor the response of the Italian authorities in relation to recommendation 8.1.1 above and to take appropriate action dependent on the response. 8.2.2 To evaluate the response of the Italian authorities to the recommendation at 8.1.5 above and to take any necessary, consequential action. 8.2.3 To consider the drafting of legislation requiring labelling, both at the wholesale and the retail level, of farmed game meat and wild game meat such that the origin of the meat (farmed or wild game) is clearly stated. 8.2.4 To clarify the requirements in relation to the authorisation and/or signature of commercial documents in all sectors where this is permitted. 8.2.5 To clarify the requirements of Council Directives 64/433/EEC7 and 71/118/EEC8 as to whether coldstore approval is required under these Directives for stores which handle only packaged fresh meat or poultry meat, and in particular, if such approvals are required if an establishment is already approved under another Directive. This should also include a prohibition on the use of string halters for horses. - Vehicles transporting animals for more than 8 hours meet the requirements of Council Regulation EC No. 411/98. In particular, vehicles transporting horses must provide: a means for segregating animals which are hostile to each other (point 1 (g) of chapter I A of the Annex of Council Directive 91/628); direct access to each compartment; and an appropriate means of watering the animals (points 3 and 6 of the Annex of Council Regulation (EC) No. 411/98). - Transporters, including those from third countries, are authorised when transporting animals within the EU, as required by Council Directive 91/628, article 5 part A paragraph 1 (a), (ii). - Facilities at staging points meet all the requirements of Council Regulation (EC) No. 1255/97 and the register of the staging point maintained as laid down in this Regulation. 8.1.3 Staff at ports should be provided with: - Appropriate facilities so that checks can be carried out as laid down in article 8 of Council Directive 91/628/EEC (as amended by 95/29/EC). - Guidance on their powers to carry out checks of sea vessels. Procedures should also be adopted for the inspection of livestock vessels so that the general requirements of Council Directive 91/628/EEC (as amended by 95/29/EC) are ensured, in particular Chapter I D of the Annex of this Directive. 8.1.4 Staff at slaughterhouses should ensure: - That animals, which are present in the lairage of a slaughterhouse for more than 12 hours, have access to water at all times as required by point 9 of chapter II of Annex A of Council Directive 93/119/EEC. - That animals in the lairage of a slaughterhouse, which may suffer if their slaughter is unduly delayed, are killed as required by point 6 of chapter I of Annex A of Council Directive 93/119/EEC. - That a back-up method of stunning is available in slaughterhouses at the point of slaughter as laid down in paragraph 2 of article 6 of Council Directive 93/119/EEC. - That string halters, which are giving rise to injuries in contravention of paragraph 1 (b) article 5A of Council Directive 91/628/EEC (as amended by 95/29/EC), are not re-circulated and that transporters who continue to use them are penalised. 8.1.5 The CCA should ensure: 20 - That only those inspections carried out to ensure that all the requirements of Council Directive 91/628/EEC (as amended by 95/29/EC) have been met are reported to the Commission, in accordance with article 8 of this Directive. - That full co-operation is provided to inspection teams as required by Commission Decision 98/139/EC. 8.2. To the Commission Services Subject to final legal assessment, the commission services should consider: 8.2.1 Opening infringement proceedings against Italy in respect of the findings of this report, in particular: - Failure to adequately pursue transporters found to be in breach of EC legislation and failure to enforce payment of penalties imposed in cases subject to legal and administrative actions. This is in contravention of Article 18 of Council Directive 91/628/EEC (as amended by 95/29/EC). - Failure to enforce the requirement for transporters, in particular those from third countries, to be authorised (article 5A paragraph 1(a) (ii) of Council Directive 91/628/EEC - as amended by 95/29/EC). - Failure to prevent the transport of animals in a way which is likely to produce suffering and failing to take account of the need to enforce Article 5A 1(b) of Council Directive 91/628/EEC (as amended by 95/29/EC). - Failure to prevent the transport of unfit animals as required by Article 3 1(b) of Council Directive 91/628/EEC (as amended by 95/29/EC). - Failure to ensure the provision of water for animals during journeys of more than eight hours as required by points 4 and 6 of the Annex of Council Regulation No. 411/98 and point 4(c) of Chapter VII of Council Directive 91/628/EEC (as amended by 95/29/EC). - Failure to ensure that horses were adequately watered in the lairages of slaughterhouses (point 9 of chapter II of Annex A of Council Directive 93/119/EEC). - Failure of certain inspections to include adequate checks of the provisions of the Directive (Article 8 of Council Directive 91/628/EEC - as amended by 95/29/EC). - Failure to ensure that journey times were respected, in particular where the animals were allowed to embark on a sea journey after having already undertaken long distance travel (Chapter VII of the Annex of Council Directive 91/628/EEC). - Failure to ensure that a back-up gun was kept at the place of slaughter (Article 6 of Council Directive 93/119/EEC) 21 8.2.2 Convening a discussion between Member States on their application of article 11 of Council Directive 91/628/EEC, in order to harmonise the interpretation of this requirement. 22 ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG (SANCO)/1105/2000 Competent authority response to the recommendations in the report 1. The competent authority submitted comments on 8 March 2001, on a draft version of this report which were taken into consideration prior to the preparation of the final report.

In these comments the Italian authorities, expressed doubts about the conclusions made regarding the following aspects: authorisations for transporters from third countries; fitness of animals for transport; ventilation requirements on vehicles; compartments in road vehicles; application of the rules of Article 5A(1)(b) of Directive 91/628/EEC (as amended); length of rest periods for animals at the Prosecco BIP; compliance of the controls at ports. However, they agreed that there is a need for further action to improve application in Italy of the rules on animal welfare during transport and made the following comments on several of the above recommendations: - Regarding 8.1.1, in accordance with the relevant Italian legislation on "Changes to the criminal system", all the appropriate procedures are being adopted in order to ensure that where a breach of the legislation occurs, the fine is paid by the transporter in question. They also pointed out that this Law provides a five year period for the Italian State to collect such fines. - Regarding 8.1.2, appropriate action will be taken to improve some of the procedures at the BIPs and staging points (watering of the animals, use of halters, etc.). In particular, assessments will be carried out to determine the best ways of meeting the requirements of horses for water during long distance transport. In addition, action will be taken to improve the compliance of operations at the approved staging points with Regulation (EC) 1255/97. - Regarding 8.1.3 the CA indicated that they would appreciate a prompt reply from the Commission to requests made for clarification on the application of Council Directive 91/628/EEC to vessels flying flags of third countries. In particular, this reply would be considered in drafting guidelines for the local authorities on the procedures to be followed regarding checks at ports and on board vessels. They also pointed out that they consider it both necessary and urgent, in the context of proposals for updating the Directive, to revise the provisions concerning sea transport, notably combined road/sea transport. - Regarding 8.1.4 appropriate action will be taken to improve procedures at slaughterhouses. - Regarding 8.1.5 improved co-operation, in accordance with the appropriate periods of notice in Directive 98/139/EC, will be assured in future provided there is more efficient and detailed planning of such missions. 23

The Commission should consider adopting safeguard measures. This should certainly be the case if one or more new outbreaks are found outside the currently affected areas, in particular where these are not linked with known outbreaks or might have been the result of illegal movements.
The Commission should continue to keep in close contact with the Italian authorities to monitor the situation so as to be able to inform the other Member States rapidly of any significant new facts.

Where necessary, the Commission should offer help to the Italian authorities, in particular by putting at their disposal the assistance of a team of experienced epidemiologists for reinforcement of the epidemiological investigations.
The Commission should carry out a new inspection before mid February 2000 to re-assess the situation and to observe the measures put in place by the Italian authorities on the basis of this report.

The Commission should take the necessary action to obtain the contingency plans foreseen in Article 17, of Council Directive 92/40/EEC from all Member States. 10.2. Recommendations to the Member State 10.2.1. Disease control measures A number of improvements or corrective actions need to be taken without any delay in order to increase the efficacy of the disease control measures and, thus, considerably decrease the risk of further spread. The Italian authorities should inform the Commission, within 5 days of receipt of the draft of this report, of the action taken in this respect. (1) Italy should put a stronger emphasis on thorough epidemiological inquiries. For this purpose, the relevant epidemiological units should be reinforced (with human and other resources). Intensive contacts between the different units should be developed or, even better, a single unit should be created in view of the multiple contacts between the two regions. The epidemiologists need to have access to all relevant information without delay and report clearly back to the authorities with possible recommendations for measures to be taken. (2) The Italian authorities should carry out preventive slaughter of poultry flocks, which as a result of the epidemiological inquiries or in view of their location, are clearly at risk of infection. (3) Permanent contact between the affected contiguous regions involved should be reinforced or, where necessary, put in place. Clear information on the results of such contacts should be available. 19 Mission report Italy - avian influenza (03 - 05.01.2000) DG(SANCO)/1112/2000-MR FINAL (4) The control measures in the different controlled zones should be reinforced. For this purpose, clear information to the public should be in place to indicate the borders of the different zones. The veterinary authorities should have close collaboration with enforcement authorities such as the "carabinieri" and the municipal police in order to increase the level and quality of surveillance and install road blocks or other means for enforcement of movement bans. (5) Intensive contacts with farmers and their organisations should be organised in order to increase their awareness of the seriousness of the situation and to improve their knowledge of the applicable control measures. As far as possible, press releases should be complemented with on-the-spot information meetings.

The organisation and functioning of the crisis centres at different levels should be more clearly specified. 10.2.2. Reporting and notification The notification of outbreaks to the Commission and the other Member States, as well as the reporting in general, need to be improved without any delay in order to decrease the risk of any spread to other countries and to allow the relevant authorities to decide whether additional safeguard measures are needed. The Italian authorities should inform the Commission, within 5 days of receipt of the draft of this report, of the action taken in this respect. (1) Italy should endeavour to centralise all information on the outbreaks in the different regions, and to constitute a list with a national numbering system. (2) The Italian CCA should follow the ADNS system (codes) in accordance with Council Directive 82/894/EEC for reporting outbreaks to the Commission and the other Member States, even when not all numerical details are completely available at the time of reporting. 10.2.3. Contingency plan In order to have a full implementation of Council Directive 92/40/EEC, Italy should, within 3 months of the receipt of the final version of this report, submit its draft contingency plan for avian influenza to the Commission, in accordance with Article 17, Paragraph 3 of this Directive. 20 Mission report Italy - avian influenza (03 - 05.01.2000) DG(SANCO)/1112/2000-MR FINAL ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)1112/2000 Competent Authority's (CA) response to the recommendations in the report In their fax of 1 March 2000, the CA has not given any indication of action taken in response to the recommendations in the report. 21

audits.title: Residues in foodstuffs of plant origin

recommendations.text: The competent authorities of Italy should ensure that a) results on inspections of plant protection products and b) results on residue monitoring are reported from every region to the central authorities within the time outlined by the specific legislation. This should be enforced, so that the information forwarded to the European Commission is complete and representative for the country.

Consideration should be given to improving co-ordination between parallel activities concerning inspections and residue monitoring by the Services of the Ministry of Health, Ministry of Agriculture and the NAS with a view to enhancing the effectiveness of the control systems.

The competent authorities should lay down clear specifications regarding sampling under the co-ordinated Community monitoring programme, in terms of exact crop-commodity sample numbers to be taken by each region. This should ensure representative sampling all over the country.

The Italian competent authorities are invited to reflect on including label checks in the inspection procedures at wholesaler and retailer level carried out by the ASL. They should ensure that results of label checks are included in the annual report in the framework of Directive 91/414/EEC from the Ministry of Health to the European Commission.

The accreditation of the laboratories carrying out pesticide residue analysis should be ensured as quickly as possible. The competent authorities should ensure that participation in the co-ordinated Community monitoring programme is restricted to laboratories which are accredited and which have participated in a previous round, or which will participate in the next round, of the European Proficiency testing. The implementation of the EU guidelines on Quality Control procedures should be encouraged.

The work towards accreditation of laboratories analysing formulations should be continued. Emphasis should be put on validation of formulation analysis methods. Taking part in Proficiency testing and working according to CIPAC methods would be desirable for the formulation laboratories.

The competent authorities should forward to the European Commission written assurances with regard to rectification of points (1) to (6) at latest 3 months after receiving the final mission report. The Italian competent authorities should provide detailed information on the actions that will be 18 taken and should propose deadlines by which these actions will be completed for the points (1),(3), (4) and (5). 7.2. To the Commission Services (1) The European Commission Services should evaluate the written assurances received from the Italian competent authorities and review the deadlines set for their completion. (2) The Commission Services should continue to provide the necessary forums for Member States, e.g. workshops, to continually revise the EU- guidelines on Quality Control procedures, in order to facilitate their application. (3) The Commission Services should ensure that only data received from accredited laboratories and from laboratories, which have participated in a previous round or will participate in the next round of the European Proficiency testing, are taken into account when compiling the EU monitoring report.

ADDENDUM Competent authority response to the recommendations in the report The competent authorities, in their comments, did not forward to the Commission concrete details of actions, which have already been taken or will be taken to implement the recommendations given in the report. 19

Competent Authorities The Competent Authorities should ensure that information on the total number of laboratories empowered to carry out aflatoxin determination in groundnuts is made available. In addition, information on the amounts of groundnuts imported or intended for import through the various Italian entry points should be made available.

Laboratory Services visited The laboratory should complete the accreditation process and obtain accreditation of the method. 12 The laboratory should participate in inter-laboratory comparison or test evaluation programs for determining aflatoxin levels. The validation report should be re-examined with regard to the data relating to the range fixed for determining aflatoxin levels and for the actual limits of determination. A procedure for the effective control of the particle size of the homogenised laboratory sample should be established. Written procedures on the uncertainty of the analytical results should be made available in order to consider the estimated uncertainty of analysis in relation to the legal use of those results.

Method of sampling Instructions on the equipment to be used and on precautions to be observed to avoid any deterioration of the sampled groundnuts should be made available. The sampling procedures should be updated, which could already brought in line with the requirements of Commission Directive 98/53/EC.

Written Assurances from the Italian Competent Authority Written assurances should be forwarded to the European Commission with regard to the rectification of points 8.1.1. to 8.1.3. The Competent Authority should provide detailed information on the actions that will be taken and propose deadlines by which these actions will be completed. 8.2. To the European Commission Services 8.2.1. Written assurances received from the Italian Competent Authority The European Commission services should evaluate the written assurances received from the Italian Competent Authority and consider the proposed deadlines for their completion. 8.2.2. Import control procedure for groundnuts intended for import The European Commission Services should consider the designation of entry ports through which all groundnuts intended for import and originated from any Third Country (not only originated from Egypt) would be subject to the required import control measures. 9. ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)/1137/2000 ­ ITALIAN COMPETENT AUTHORITY RESPONSE TO THE RECOMMENDATIONS IN THE REPORT 9.1. Response to recommendations given to the Competent Authorities The Italian Competent Authority responded, proposing deadlines for completion, as follows: 13 - An investigation is currently under way to determine the number of laboratories capable of carrying out analyses of aflatoxins in groundnuts. - The amended method of analysis and its validation will presumably accredited following an inspection by SINAL. - The visited laboratory has undertaken to participate in inter-laboratory tests on determining aflatoxin levels. Furthermore, procedures will be established to monitor the particle size of the laboratory samples. - The sampling procedures will be updated and precautions will be taken to avoid any deterioration in groundnut samples. 14
The Commission services should review the conditions concerning serological testing before movement in order to allow the competent authorities to concentrate on other aspects of disease control.

The Commission services should reflect upon the possibility to introduce a proposal for amendments to Council Directive 92/40/EEC, as referred to under point 7.3. 8.2. Recommendations to the Member State A number of further improvements or corrective actions need to be taken in order to increase the efficacy of the disease control measures and, hence, considerably decrease the risk of further spread. The Italian authorities should inform the Commission, within 10 days of receipt of the draft of this report, of the action taken in this respect, or in the case of the checklist referred to in point (1) below, of the timetable for completion. (1) Italy should endeavour to further improve the epidemiological inquiries. Immediate action should be taken to improve the effectiveness and speed of communication, and to refine questioning techniques. In the longer term, the competent authorities should review the checklist used for this in the light of the experiences gained. (2) Further improvement is also needed in relation to day-to-day contacts concerning control measures between the affected contiguous regions. In particular, clear information on the results of such contacts should be available.

The control measures in the different controlled zones should be further reinforced. For this purpose, further improvements are necessary to indicate more clearly the borders of the different zones to the public. The veterinary authorities should reinforce their collaboration with enforcement authorities such as the "carabinieri" or other police forces in order to increase the level and quality of surveillance and install road blocks or other means for enforcement of movement bans.

Intensive contacts with farmers and their organisations, as well as with other operators involved such as hauliers and managers of egg packaging stations, slaughterhouses or feed mills, should be continued in order to increase their awareness of the seriousness of the situation and to improve their knowledge of the applicable control measures further.

The backlog in communicating data to the Commission and the other Member States in accordance with ADNS should be eliminated. 29 Mission report Italy - avian influenza (15 - 18.02.2000) DG(SANCO)/1161/2000-MR Final ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)/1161/2000 Competent Authority's (CA) response to the recommendations in the report The CA have made, in their fax of 18 April 2000, certain additional points which they would like to see included in the mission report. Some of these points give an update of the epidemiological situation at the time of sending the email, while others give some further clarifications to the text. No specific information was added indicating any corrective action taken by the Italian CA after the mission apart from the improvement of the ADNS backlog (recommendation n° 5). 30

December 2000 by making sure that the sampling and the visual inspections are done or at least at all stages supervised by official plant health inspectors. Additional auxiliary staff that might be required for the sampling and for the visual inspections in the peak season, should be employed by and under the responsibility of the official plant protection service; (6) create a formal arrangement including requirements for appropriate record keeping, between the official plant protection service and the reference laboratory for R. solanacearum and C.m.s. from 1 December 2000; 23 (7) improve the deficiencies in the analytical procedures identified at the private laboratory involved in testing Egyptian potatoes without delay and consider to carry out all confirmation tests for R. solanacearum in official laboratories; (8) audit the performance of private laboratories involved in plant health checks by randomly double checking samples in official laboratories of the regional plant protection services from 1 January 2001. The central competent authority in Italy is requested to report to the Commission by 31 January 2001 on action taken and planned on the above points. 24 ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)/1163/2000 Competent Authority response to the recommendations in the report The Italian Ministero per le Politiche Agricole e Forestali (MiPAF) indicated that "the recommendations are noted and the European Commission will be informed of the action taken as requested and by the date specified". The plant disease observatory in Trieste informed the Commission that regardi s 5 to 8, "a formal request has been made for transfer to the observatory of two agronomists or agricultural science graduates, possibly qualified as plant health inspectors and having a knowledge of the specific field of plant pathology. It is confirmed that "double checking" has been practised as of this year." 25
The Commission should continue to keep in close contact with the Italian authorities to monitor the situation so as to be able to inform the other Member States rapidly of any significant new facts.

The Commission services should consider the possibility of introducing a proposal for amendments to Council Directive 90/539/EEC, including in the models of certificates laid down in Annex IV, a clause concerning the vaccination status of the birds or the flocks of origin.

The Commission services should consider addressing deficiencies in import and intra-Community trade certificates accompanying poultry and/or hatching eggs with the competent authorities of the countries of origin. 9.2. Recommendations to the Member State A number of improvements or corrective actions need to be taken in order to increase the efficacy of the disease control measures and, hence, considerably decrease the risk of further spread. The Italian authorities should inform the Commission, within 10 days of receipt of the draft of this report, of the action taken in this respect, or, where applicable, of the timetable for completion. (1) Real crisis units should be established at the different levels and in the different regions concerned. (2) Reinforcement of the staff dealing with the disease control at certain levels, in particular at national level should immediately be arranged. (3) Italy should endeavour to improve the effectiveness and speed of communication between different competent authorities involved. Further improvement is also needed in relation to day-to-day contacts concerning control measures between the affected contiguous regions. In particular, clear information on the results of such contacts should be available.

The control measures in the different controlled zones should be further reinforced. For this purpose, further improvements are necessary to indicate more clearly the borders of the different zones to the public. The veterinary authorities should reinforce their collaboration with enforcement authorities such as the "carabinieri" or other police forces in order to increase the level and quality of surveillance.

The competent authorities should take action to ensure that the official veterinarians rigorously respect the Community provisions with regard to health marking of poultry meat from restricted zones. 27
The backlog in communicating data to the Commission and the other Member States in accordance with ADNS should be further reduced.

In order to have a full implementation of Council Directive 92/66/EEC, Italy should, within 3 months of the receipt of the final version of this report, submit its draft contingency plan for Newcastle disease to the Commission services, in accordance with Article 21, Paragraph 3 of this Directive.

The competent authorities should consider addressing deficiencies in import and intra-Community trade certificates accompanying poultry and/or hatching eggs with the competent authorities of the countries of origin. 28 ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG (SANCO)/1195/2000 Competent Authority's (CA) response to the recommendations in the report The CA have not made any comments on the report within the foreseen deadlines or supplied any indication of corrective actions they wish to undertake. To inform immediately the remaining Regions of the outcome of the mission. To ensure a strengthening of veterinary supervision at all levels, in order to monitor satisfactorily the compliance of the establishments with EU requirements. To rectify deficiencies in relation to structure/layout, maintenance, equipment cleanliness and operational hygiene encountered in the plants visited and ensure that similar deficiencies receive attention in all other plants. 20

The major deficiencies related to the procedures (identification and selection, procedure and ship supplier supervision) should be corrected immediately and in particular: § Italy should ensure that veterinary checks on consignments of live animals and products are carried out in accordance with the requirements laid down in Directive 97/78/EC and Directive 91/496/EEC and related Decisions, in particular it should ensure the presence of veterinary staff during the unloading of live animals and the veterinary checks for live animals in transit arriving in Prosecco-Fernetti road. § Italy should ensure that the staff in the BIPs improve their systems for obtaining information on incoming and outgoing consignments and take an active part in order to guarantee that all consignments related to veterinary checks from third countries arriving in the BIPs are under the supervision of the official veterinarians and are checked in accordance with the import requirements to this. It should be also focused on the veterinary supervision of the ship suppliers. § Italy should ensure that the veterinary checks are carried out in Bari in compliance with the requirements laid down in the relevant legislation and that the facilities fulfil those requirements.

Action should be taken to correct all other deficiencies noted in this report (general findings, veterinary staff, facilities, equipment, hygiene, documentation, registration, identification and selection, procedure, kitchen waste and transit/ship supplier procedures). In any event all deficiencies should be corrected within three months of receipt of the translated final report and in particular: §BIP staff: Shortage of staff in Livorno-Pisa port, Milano-Malpensa, Gorizia and Prosecco-Fernetti road and adequate training for the staff in each BIP in especially in relation to procedures and systems for identification and selection of consignments. § Facilities: The minor deficiencies related to the construction of the facilities in Milano-Malpensa, Torino-Caselle, Gorizia and in Prosecco-Fernetti road for live animals should be corrected. § Procedures: Veterinary checks on transit consignments exiting the EU to the Vatican City State have to be ensured. 23/02/01 - 56367 Page 25 of 29 DG (SANCO)/1264/2000 ­ MR Final

ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)/1264/2000 Statements of the Competent Authority to the recommendations in this report 9.1. Response to recommendation 8.1.1. Immediate instructions were issued to Bari to remedy the serious shortcomings found in its facilities and procedures. The authorisation for HC-products has been limited to packed products (HC(2)) until the new facilities are completed and commissioned. An inspection in Bari carried out by the competent authority showed that cargo manifests are checked since mid October 2000 and that veterinary checks are made on the ship supplier. The new facilities have been altered to provide ambient temperature storage in the HC-unit and a dock shelter system is on order. The assembly of the cold rooms will be completed until 10.02.2001. The facilities currently in use have been cleaned and completely cleared of extraneous material. Some of the missing equipment has been made available in the inspection room. A further inspection is planned by 15.02.2001 to verify that the requirements have been fully met. 9.2. Response to recommendation 8.1.2. The matter regarding the Official Journal Notice No 1999/C 356/02 has been brought to the notice of the Ministry of the Environment with a view to producing a list of places of introduction and export similar to that already existing for other Member States. To issue the protocol for official controls without further delay. This protocol should include sufficient details as to the frequency of official controls, the checks to be applied, corrective actions and records to be kept on the control activities.

These instructions should be detailed enough to ensure that reconciliation checks are able to detect discrepancies, appropriate corrective action is taken and discrepancies are reported up to the level of central competent authority.

The central competent authority as well as the regional veterinary services should continue their internal audits. The Central competent authorities should take action to harmonise the implementation of the total feed ban. The Central competent authorities should verify that all the plants approved for the incorporation of PAP have been inspected and the requirements of Commission Decision 2001/9/EC are met in each plant. 36 3. The co-operation of the different bodies involved in the verification of the proper implementation of the feed ban should be improved in order to ensure effective use of resources. A specific National program for animal feed controls - including the tasks and responsibilities of all the authorities involved and clear risk based targeting - should be seriously considered as an instrument to avoid overlapping controls and increase the efficiency of the controls.

The National Program for animal feed should give more consideration to the necessity to provide the regional Veterinary Services with clear criteria for selecting farms to be inspected and where samples must be taken.
The Competent authority should consider increasing the number of samples taken from raw materials.

With regard to epidemio-surveillance: 1. The budgetary provisions allowing a continued training effort - as already recommended by the previous mission - should be made without further delay. The Central Competent Authority should take action ­ including the training activities mentioned above ­ to ensure that all clinical suspects including bovines placed under '15 days observation' are notified to Regional Veterinary Services and subsequently to the Central Competent Authority. An inspection programme has been launched to audit SRM related control activities in slaughterhouses, temporary storage facilities and pre-treatment plants. The new office (see point 1) will be responsible for supervising the activities of the Regions, carrying out audits, verifying the proper implementation of provisions and the inspection activities. 5. The control plan for the year 2002 will include better defined sampling methods and procedures. While drafting the control plan the recommendations of the mission report will be taken into consideration. 6. The number of samples from feed materials will be increased.
The National Health Institute has been invited to organise a ring-test in order to verify and refine the diagnostic technique currently in use for the detection of MBM in animal feed.

Training courses for local and regional veterinary services have started in June 2001. Following these courses the local veterinary services will then organise training for practitioners, farmer, hauliers etc.).

Meetings with veterinary practitioners, stock-farmers' associations and other associations of the production chain are foreseen shortly in order to discuss the problems with the notification of suspected clinical cases. These problems will also be addressed during the training courses for local and regional veterinary services. Moreover, the surveillance system will be amended in such a way that suspect cases will be notified to the competent central authority already at the beginning of an observation period. 38

Verona : For the purposes of identification and selection of consignments, contacts have been established with the airport customs authorities, which have confirmed their full availability as soon as the BIP is officially authorised to carry out checks. 6.1 : The head of the Verona regional office has made arrangements for staff training with a view to fully complying with the procedures laid down in Council Directive 97/78/EC. 11 6.2 : The competent office of the Directorate-General ensures all forms of useful cooperation with all regional offices on a daily basis in order to resolve any problems arising in connection with import controls. 6.10 : Taken in to account the facilities in place, both BIPs are requested to be approved for products of animal origin for human and non human consumption on the condition that they are packed (HC(2)-NHC(2)) and for a volume that will be less than 500 consignments per year. 12
To reflect on the new roles and tasks of planning, coordination and supervision of each authority in the field of animal nutrition after the decentralisation process13.

To review the number of staff allocated in relation to the above-mentioned tasks and to provide them with adequate targeted training, in order to ensure full compliance with Directives 95/53/EC and 95/69/EC. With regard to the official inspections in the field of animal nutrition:

To ensure that Art 4 of Directive 95/53/EC (performance of inspections) is complied with, in particular: ­ That the risks and experience gained from every source of information (PNAA and any other official inspections, Commissio s in the field of animal nutrition and the rapid alert system) are taken into account in the design of PNAA. ­ That all animal feed stages are taken into account by PNAA (inspection in all establishments and intermediaries in the animal feed sector in PNAA, even if they are not covered by Directive 95/69/EC, and inspection on imported feed products, specifying the type and frequency of checks). ­ That, in the framework of PNAA, analyses of dioxins on feed materials and feedingstuffs are performed. ­ That an amendment of PNAA is considered, introducing more detailed instruction to the Regions and rationale grounds on which the number of samples and type of analysis are based. ­ That guidelines are produced which, together with the above-mentioned version of PNAA, would ensure its harmonised implementation, to guarantee that the experience and information on the risks from the different regional services is comparable and can be properly assessed. ­ That access at central and regional level are gained on relevant data from all inspections (provided by local and regional veterinary services, laboratories, NAS, MPAF and any other), and made available to all interested parties in the field on animal nutrition. ­ That PNAA foresees any additional controls that could be performed by the local veterinary services, providing common criteria for the consistent implementation and adequate supervision of these activities.

To provide adequate instructions in relation to the actions to be taken in case of non- compliance and to monitor these precisely in order to ensure full compliance with Art 19 of Directive 95/53/EC. 13 In their response to the draft report the Italian authorities stated that the decentralisation process is still under way, and that only after its completion a rationale planning of the supervision of each authority will be possible. 20

To ensure that Art 18(2) of Directive 95/53/EC (drawing up a list of laboratories carrying out analyses and ensuring that such laboratories are designated on account of their capabilities) is complied with, in particular: ­ That the technical capability of all the regional laboratories in charge of official analyses is guaranteed. To this end, an adequate level of supervision of such laboratories should be provided, including the appropriateness of the flow of information, testing capacity and policy applied on inconclusive results. ­ That confirmation of positive results from laboratories that are UNI EN 45000 accredited is performed by laboratories accredited to the same standard.

To ensure that Chapter II of Directive 95/53/EC (imports from third countries) is complied with, in particular: ­ That all feed products are subjected to the proper checks when they are introduced into the customs territory of the Community. ­ That checks on feed products are applied to the same level irrespective of the official body in charge of controls. ­ That sound information is provided to the responsible authority in order to issue the standard document referred to in Art 9(1) of Directive 95/53/EC. With regard to the approval and registration of establishments and intermediaries (E/I) operating in the animal feed sector:

To ensure that Art 21(1) of Directive 95/69/EC (adopting administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive) is fully applied, in particular: ­ That appropriate guidelines and enhance coordination between the different authorities involved are provided, in order to have a common understanding and a harmonised implementation of the inspections to verify and check compliance with the requirements that should be met by E/I. ­ That the authorisation activity is appropriately supervised to guarantee that the above-mentioned common criteria are effectively complied with. ­ That unequivocal guidelines on possible non-compliance and actions that should be taken to address them are produced, and the implementation of these rules properly supervised. ­ That a comprehensive knowledge of the E/I authorisation status in gained at regional and central level. ­ That the authorisation process of E/I is completed in a reasonable time.

To ensure that representatives importing some feed products comply with the requirements established in Art 6(2) of Directive 98/51/EC, in particular in relation to forbidden additives and additives whose authorisations is linked to a given company, and to draw up the list of representatives and manufacturer according to the requirements of this Directive. The competent authorities are invited to provide details of the actions taken and planned, including deadlines for their completion: ­ within 25 working days following the receipt of the draft report, in response to recommendations nº 6 and 8 concerning the checks on imports of feed products and intermediaries importing some feed products, respectively, ­ within 25 working days following the receipt of the final report, in response to the others recommendations. 21 ADDENDUM Response of the competent authorities to the recommendations Comments from the Italian CCA on the draft report were received on 10 January 2003, and included an outline of the actions planned and/or undertaken to address the recommendations contained in the report. These may be summarised as follows: To recommendation number: 3. The analysis of dioxins in feedingstuffs will be included in the PNNA from 2003 on. Some meetings will be organised with the ICRF, NAS and RVS in the next months, in order to plan the control activities and to improve the flow of information. 3, 7. A permanent working group for animal nutrition will be created with the regional authorities, with the following main objectives: ­ To draw a new, more detailed PNAA, which will take into account the risk and experience gained and, when possible, Commissio s on the coordinated inspection programme in animal nutrition. ­ To draw up guidelines for the implementation of Directives 95/53/EC and 95/69/EC, which will be distributed among the operators in the sector at national level. 4. The new PNAA will provide adequate instructions in relation to the actions to be taken in case of non-compliance. 6. The legal void in the check on feed products imported from third countries will be covered by the transposition of Directives 2000/77/EC and 2001/46/EC. A new legislative decree will be produced soon (in substitution of decree 460/99), in which the competence for checks and the issuing of the standard document referred to in Art

(1) of Directive 95/53/EC will be attributed to the BIPs. In addition, criteria on the type and frequency of these checks will be produced. 7. The new PNAA will foresee the reporting of the additional controls performed by the LVS to the RVS and CCA, twice a year, which will provide a complete overview of the national situation and to plan the future activity. Steps have been taken by the new Unit in charge of the animal feed sector in order to enhance coordination between the different authorities involved. In addition, the programme of inspections that the RVS started last year will continue, according to the available resources. ____________________ 22
The major deficiencies related to the facilities for products (Salerno, Napoli port and aiport, Venezia port and Olbia) should be corrected within 6 months of receipt of the translated final report.
The major deficiencies related to the facilities for live animals in La Spezia should be corrected within 1 month of receipt of the translated final report.

Action should be taken to correct all other major and minor deficiencies noted in the report, mainly related to the general findings, staff, training, facilities, 27 OJ L 323, 26.11.1997, pp 31 - 36 28 Prot. 600.3/UVC.1/1333 of 18.03.2003 13 equipment, hygiene, documentation, registration, identification and selection of consignments, procedures, transit and kitchen waste. This should be done within 3 months of the receipt of the translated final report. 8.2. TO THE COMMISSION SERVICES 1. Consider amending the approvals for the BIPs mentioned in points 8.1.1. and 8.1.2. if satisfactory guarantees are not provided within the indicated time limit. 2. Consider amending the approval for the following BIPs: ­ Napoli port: withdrawal of IC 2 (Magazzini Tirreni ­ Molo Pisacane), ­ Venezia airport: amend approval to HC (2), NHC-T(CH)(2), NHC-NT(2), ­ Venezia port: withdrawal of IC 2. 3. Consider limiting the approval for the BIPs of Salerno, Napoli port and airport, Venezia airport and Livorno-Pisa airport to packed products if satisfactory guarantees are not provided within the indicated time limit.

Consider appropriate follow-up action in the light of the actions planned/ undertaken in response to recommendation 8.1.3. ______________________ 14 ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)/9031/2003 In response to the recommendations in the draft report, the Central Competent Authority (CCA) in Italy indicated the followi under point 8.1.3: In this context, CCA will issue precise instructions to those BIPs where shortcomings have been noted in order that Community law is complied with as laid down, and provide an action plan within one month of receiving the translation of the final report.
